_note: The tracked set. 'sensitivity' is a signed prior from -1 to +1: if that driver RISES, this is the direction the asset is expected to go. These are opinions and are labelled as such on the page - they get checked against, and eventually corrected by, the measured reactions in data/reactions.csv. 'overnight' names the contract to use for the Asia session when the primary symbol does not trade overnight.

gold.name: Gold
gold.what: Spot gold, quoted per troy ounce. Pays no yield, so it is priced almost entirely off the opportunity cost of holding it and off demand for a store of value outside the banking system.
gold.drives_it: Real yields first, the dollar second, haven demand third. Central bank buying is the slow structural bid underneath all of it.

sp500.name: S&P 500
sp500.what: The broad US equity market, and the reference risk asset for everything else.
sp500.drives_it: Earnings and the discount rate. Growth helps until it forces policy tighter, at which point it stops helping.

nasdaq.name: Nasdaq 100
nasdaq.what: Large-cap growth and technology. Longer duration cash flows than the S&P, which makes it the more rate-sensitive of the two.
nasdaq.drives_it: The same forces as the S&P, but the discount rate matters more and current earnings matter less.

oil.name: WTI crude
oil.what: US benchmark crude. The one asset here where physical supply genuinely sets the price rather than expectations about it.
oil.drives_it: Supply first, demand second. It is also the transmission belt from geopolitics into inflation, which is why it matters far beyond energy.

dollar.name: Dollar index
dollar.what: The dollar against a basket of major currencies. The unit almost everything else is priced in.
dollar.drives_it: US rates relative to everywhere else. It is also a haven, which is why it can rise both when things are good and when they are frightening.

us10y.name: US 10-year yield
us10y.what: The yield, not the price - so it moves opposite to the bond. The single most important number in global finance.
us10y.drives_it: Expected policy plus expected inflation plus a term premium for the risk of being wrong about either.

silver.name: Silver
silver.what: Half precious metal, half industrial input. Behaves like a leveraged, noisier gold with a growth kicker attached.
silver.drives_it: Everything that moves gold, amplified, plus genuine industrial demand - solar and electronics in particular.

copper.name: Copper
copper.what: The cleanest market read on global industrial activity there is, which is why it is nicknamed the metal with a doctorate.
copper.drives_it: Growth, mostly Chinese. Mine supply matters at the margin and occasionally dominates.

bitcoin.name: Bitcoin
bitcoin.what: Traded as the highest-beta liquidity asset in the set. Whether it is also a store of value is an argument, not a fact - so this database treats it as what it demonstrably behaves like.
bitcoin.drives_it: Liquidity and risk appetite, overwhelmingly. Its correlation with gold is unstable and should be checked rather than assumed.

eurusd.name: EUR/USD
eurusd.what: The most traded currency pair. Effectively the inverse of the dollar index with a European growth story attached.
eurusd.drives_it: The gap between US and euro-area rate expectations, plus relative growth.

usdjpy.name: USD/JPY
usdjpy.what: The purest expression of rate differentials in the currency market, and the funding leg of the global carry trade.
usdjpy.drives_it: US yields against Japanese ones. The yen is also a haven, so risk-off drags this pair down hard - and carry unwinds here have a habit of moving everything else.

vix.name: VIX
vix.what: Thirty-day implied volatility on the S&P. A price for insurance, not a forecast - it says what protection costs, not what will happen.
vix.drives_it: Demand for hedges. Mean-reverting by construction, which is why a high VIX is usually a poor reason to expect more trouble.
